description: 2 tactical challenges for Black against the Orthoschnapp Gambit. Retreat with 4...Bg6! and keep the bishop.

drills.briefExplanation: 3...Bf5 4.Bd3 Bg6! — develop, then retreat; the bishop stays on its best diagonal.
drills.description: Black to play. White is threatening the Orthoschnapp 4.Bd3 — develop 3...Bf5 and be ready to retreat.
drills.explanation: The antidote to the Orthoschnapp: after 3...Bf5 4.Bd3, Black simply retreats 4...Bg6! — keeping the light-squared bishop on its best diagonal. White's 4.Bd3 achieved nothing (the bishop just steps back), Black's Caro-Kann structure is intact, and White spent a tempo. Don't trade your best piece when you can keep it.
drills.name: The Bg6 Retreat

drills.briefExplanation: 4...Bg6 5.Qe2 e6 6.Nf3 Nd7 — retreat, solidify, and develop the knight.
drills.description: Black to play. White challenged with 4.Bd3 — retreat and complete development.
drills.explanation: The full defensive scheme: 4...Bg6 keeps the bishop, and after 5.Qe2 e6 Black solidifies the center. 6...Nd7 next develops with tempo toward e5 or c5 — Black's Caro-Kann is rock solid, the bishop still eyes the queenside, and White's 'gambit' never won the bishop pair. Patience beats provocation.
drills.name: Keeping the Bishop
